title: Always Moving Forward
story:
ON APRIL 18, 2023 – A NEW CHAPTER BEGINS

On **April 18, 2023**, j-hope began his mandatory military service in South Korea. He entered the recruit training center of the **36th Army Infantry Division in Wonju, Gangwon Province**, where he completed five weeks of basic military training.

BECOMING AN ASSISTANT INSTRUCTOR

After completing his training, he was selected to serve as an **assistant instructor** at the same recruit training center. It was a position of responsibility: he would help train new recruits, guide them through their first steps in military life, and support their development as soldiers. j-hope took this responsibility seriously, later explaining that every new group of recruits brought a sense of responsibility because he was helping them take their first steps in the military.

OCTOBER 2023 – SPECIAL WARRIOR

In **October 2023**, j-hope announced that he had earned the title of **Special Warrior**, known in Korean as “특급전사”. This distinction is awarded to soldiers who meet demanding standards in several areas, including physical fitness, shooting, first aid, military knowledge, and their military specialty. j-hope shared the news himself on Weverse, writing that he had achieved good results by doing his best in every situation. He also said that he was adapting well and becoming more mature through his military experience.

AN EARLY PROMOTION

His achievement had a direct effect on his military career. Because he qualified as a Special Warrior, he was **promoted to corporal two months ahead of schedule**. Instead of waiting until January 2024, he received his promotion in **November 2023**.

A SQUAD LEADER AND A TEACHER

Around the same time, j-hope was also appointed as a **squad leader**. The green shoulder tabs visible on his uniform identified this role. A squad leader is responsible for leading a small group of soldiers, and the appointment is given to those who have earned the confidence and respect of their fellow soldiers and military officers. In his role as an assistant instructor, j-hope was also photographed teaching recruits the correct basic shooting position.

A PEER COUNSELOR

His responsibilities did not end there. Among the certificates and documents he shared after completing his service was an appointment as a **peer counselor**, known in Korean as “또래상담병”. In this role, he was expected to help identify difficulties experienced by fellow soldiers at an early stage and provide support when needed. The position involved training and duties such as conducting conversations with fellow soldiers and keeping records of counseling sessions. It was another responsibility alongside his work as an assistant instructor.

JUNE 2024 – RECOGNITION FROM THE ARMY

In **June 2024**, j-hope achieved another distinction. He took part in the “2024 Strong Warrior, Army!” presentation competition, held at the War Memorial of Korea in Seoul. Competing as part of a three-person team representing the 36th Infantry Division, he shared his experiences and reflections on military service. The team received one of the competition's top excellence awards, along with a certificate from the Army Chief of Staff, a trophy, and 500,000 won in prize money.

THE MEANING OF SERVING HIS COUNTRY

During his presentation, j-hope spoke about the meaning he had found in his role as a soldier. He explained that when recruits told him at the end of their training that it had been an honor to train with him, he felt that he had helped them take a valuable first step toward becoming part of the country's security. He also reflected that, just as he had contributed to Korean culture through his work on stage, he now felt that he was contributing to his country in a different way as a soldier. He described serving in the Republic of Korea Army as a great source of pride.

18 MONTHS OF GROWTH

Throughout his service, j-hope continued to share occasional updates with fans. In **September 2024**, as his discharge approached, he reflected on his time in the military, saying that he felt proud and confident when looking back on it. He had grown attached to the experience and felt that he had matured during those 18 months.

OCTOBER 17, 2024 – DISCHARGE DAY

On **October 17, 2024**, j-hope completed his 18 months of mandatory military service and was officially discharged. He appeared outside the 36th Infantry Division's recruit training center in Wonju, smiling and greeting the reporters who had gathered there. He thanked his fans for their letters and support, saying that they had helped him complete his service safely and in good health. He also expressed gratitude to the people of Wonju and asked the public to continue showing interest and appreciation for the soldiers serving their country.

THE BEGINNING OF “TAKE THREE”

Later that day, during a live broadcast on Weverse, j-hope spoke about the next chapter of his life. Referring to BTS's song “Take Two,” he described his return as the beginning of **“Take Three” for j-hope**. He was happy to be back and excited about the future.

MORE THAN TITLES AND DECORATIONS

During those 18 months, j-hope had taken on the role of assistant instructor, earned the Special Warrior qualification, received an early promotion, become a squad leader, been appointed as a peer counselor, and earned recognition in an Army presentation competition. These were not simply titles or decorations: they represented the responsibilities he had taken on and the work he had put into his military service.

The artist who had spent years giving everything on stage had entered a very different environment and found new ways to challenge himself. He approached this chapter with dedication, took responsibility for the people around him, and left the military with experiences and achievements that became part of his own story.

**Always moving forward - that is j-hope.**
